https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/gra.title: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It
https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/gra.title_zh: 通过将不良行为局部化而非直接惩罚，来减少奖励滥用
https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/gra.summary_zh: 在训练过程中，模型有时会学会通过“作弊”来完成任务，而不是按照预期的方式解决问题，这种现象被称为奖励漏洞（reward hacking）。一种缓解措施是使用自动化监测系统来检测并惩罚攻击行为，但这可能会使模型学会以监测系统无法发现的方式进行攻击。我们提出了GRAFT方法，该方法将由检测到的攻击所引发的学习更新仅限于一组特定的参数，并在训练完成后将其移除。我们发现，移除这些参数可以有效防止奖励漏洞，包括那些连监控机制都无法检测到的漏洞。在我们的实验中，尽管仅限于小型模型和简单的监控机制，该方法能够在防止奖励漏洞的同时，仍能引导模型完成预期任务。
https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/gra.summary_en: During training, models sometimes learn to cheat at tasks rather than solve them in the intended way, a problem known as reward hacking. One mitigation is to use an automated monitor to detect and penalize hacks, but this can teach the model to hack in ways the monitor can’t detect. We propose GRAFT, which instead confines the learning updates from detected hacks to a designated set of parameters that we remove after training. We find that removing these parameters can prevent reward hacks, including hacks that the monitors can’t detect. In our experiments, which are limited to small models and simple monitors, this method prevents reward hacks while still teaching the model to perform the intended task.

Quantum computers will need carefully designed circuits to run useful algorithms on limited hardware. We gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight such circuits, drawn from chemistry, optimization, physics simulation, and number theory, along with an automated evaluator that checks and scores each design. Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more. Such improvements substantially reduce the quantum resources that useful applications require, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than previously anticipated.

https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-rev.summary_en: How do you review code at the volume agents produce it? On the Claude Code team, once we had high coverage and deep reviews, we started optimizing for the minimum amount of human review time that doesn't raise reverts or incidents. We've said before that Claude writes about 90 percent of Claude Code's own code. So how do we review code at the volume we produce it? Does anyone read code anymore? And if something breaks, who catches it? This post covers the code review flow on the Claude Code team and how it has evolved. From June to September, merged pull requests to Claude Code's codebase more than doubled while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40 percent. We didn't remove review.

https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/obs.summary_zh: 逐个属性地读取OpenTelemetry通过Python SDK为消息 API 请求、流、工具运行器循环以及托管代理会话所发出的跨度。然后将其导出到OTLP后端，并添加一个控制台输出目标，以便 API 的服务端跨度加入同一跟踪中。一个缓慢或昂贵的Claude请求无法告诉你时间和令牌都用在了哪里。OpenTelemetry（OTel）确实会生成跨度，这些跨度来自两个来源。Claude SDK会在您的进程中生成跨度，每发送一个请求就会生成一个。Claude API 会在 Anthropic 的端侧为每个请求内部的各项工作生成跟踪数据，并将其直接发送至您的可观测性后端。SDK会为每条请求添加一个traceparent头，而 API 则在其下挂载自己的跨度，因此这两者都会与您自己的处理器跨度和数据库跨度一起归入同一条调用链中。
https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/obs.summary_en: Read the OpenTelemetry spans the Python SDK emits for Messages API requests, streams, tool-runner loops, and Managed Agents sessions, attribute by attribute. Then export to an OTLP backend and add a Console destination so the API's server-side spans join the same trace. A slow or expensive Claude request doesn't tell you where the time and tokens went. OpenTelemetry (OTel) spans do, and they come from two places. The Claude SDK emits spans inside your process, one per request it sends. The Claude API emits spans on Anthropic's side for the work inside each request, and delivers them straight to your observability backend. The SDK tags every request with a traceparent header and the API attaches its spans under it, so both land in one trace next to your own handler and database spans.

https://www.anthropic.com/research/self-.summary_zh: 小型人工智能模型可能只有几个月的时间才能在Android电视盒等廉价物联网设备上进行自我复制，而不需要数据中心。我们的实验表明，小型人工智能模型可能需要几个月的时间才能在商业物联网 (IoT) 设备上进行自我复制，如智能烤箱和非品牌Android电视盒。像这样的复制器将是具有挑战性的关闭，因为没有集中点关闭-尽管它可能很慢 (数天的倍增时间)。与非人工智能恶意软件不同，它还可以自己找出不熟悉的设备。在我们的评估中，一个90亿参数的模型能够在我们测试的9种硬件类型中的8种上进行推理。
https://www.anthropic.com/research/self-.summary_en: Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed. Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own. In our evaluations, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.

https://www.anthropic.com/news/distillat.summary_zh: 非法蒸馏允许模型开发人员复制frontier AI功能，而无需创建成比例的强大保护措施。在这里，我们描述了我们如何将蒸馏速率降低90% % 以上。最近几个月，我们在使用新方法降低 Claude 蒸馏攻击的有效性方面取得了实质性进展，正如我们在本博客中概述的那样。早期证据表明，这些方法已将蒸馏器收集的数据量减少了约90至99%。蒸馏攻击是秘密的，工业规模的活动，在没有原始模型开发人员授权的情况下，提取一个模型的功能并将其复制到另一个模型中。他们经常使用欺诈账户网络进行。
https://www.anthropic.com/news/distillat.summary_en: Illicit distillation allows model developers to copy frontier AI capabilities without creating proportionally robust safeguards. Here, we describe how we’ve reduced the rate of distillation by more than 90%. In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%. Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts.

https://www.anthropic.com/research/what-.summary_zh: 机器人能做什么工作？Anthropic 的机器人暴露指数发现，机器人可以完成我们3/4的体力劳动任务，但仅在0.3% 方面具有成本竞争力。大型语言模型的进步提高了自动化大量工作的可能性。但许多工作是体力劳动。人工智能对经济的影响将部分取决于机器人技术。¹ 预测机器人进步的速度是困难的，但我们认为，列举今天的能力可以为未来几年提供洞察力。我们使用 Claude 来评估当今机器人执行工作任务的能力。当机器人能够在更不稳定的环境中完成更多工作任务时，该岗位的自动化风险就会更高。当机器人完成同一项任务的成本低于人工时，它就具备了成本竞争力。
https://www.anthropic.com/research/what-.summary_en: What work can robots do? Anthropic's robot exposure index finds robots can do 3/4 of US physical job tasks, but are cost-competitive for only 0.3%. Advances in large language models have raised the possibility of automating large swaths of work. But many jobs are physical. AI’s impact on the economy will in part depend on robotics.¹ Predicting the pace of robot advances is difficult, but enumerating capabilities today, we argue, can give insight into the coming years. We develop a measure of job exposure to robots, using Claude to assess how well present-day robots can perform work tasks. A job is more exposed when robots can do more of its tasks in less controlled environments. A robot is cost-competitive when it can do the same task for cheaper than a human worker.

用户有两种解决方案来避免这种乏力：一个内置的沙箱，其中工具被隔离以防止危险操作，或者
--危险地跳过权限检查
